title: 2024 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: Cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has lengths \(BC=CD=3\) and \(DA=5\) with \(\angle CDA=120^\circ.\) What is the length of the shorter diagonal of \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text:
In \(\triangle ACD,\) the law of cosines gives \(AC^2=9+25-2(15)\cos120^\circ\) \(=34+15=49,\) so \(AC=7.\)

Since \(ABCD\) is cyclic, \(\angle ABC=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ.\) In \(\triangle ABC\) with \(BC=3\) and \(AC=7,\) the law of cosines gives \(49=AB^2+9-3AB,\) so \(AB=8.\) By Ptolemy, \(AC\cdot BD=AB\cdot CD+BC\cdot DA\) \(=8\cdot3+3\cdot5=39,\) hence \(BD=\tfrac{39}{7}.\) This is shorter than \(AC=7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Find \(AB\) using \(\angle ABC=60^\circ,\) then apply Ptolemy: \(AC\cdot BD=AB\cdot CD+BC\cdot DA\)
